analysis.title: Weekly Markets Monitor, 2 November 2026: Leveraged repricers
key_insights: Gold's recent weakness is attributed to a repricing of the Fed's expected rate path since the October meeting, plus some rotation back into bonds. The report says selling appears driven by leveraged investors, while US gold ETF flows have been fairly benign.
The LBMA Gold Price PM closed Friday at US$3,913/oz, down 2.5% w/w and below US$4,000/oz for the first time since mid-July. Year-to-date gold is down 10.4%.

COMEX positioning: Managed Money positions have fallen about 11t since mid-October. Other Reportable, Non-Reportable and Spreading positions have dropped about 70t. The report says COMEX futures may have had a stronger hand in price moves than usual in recent weeks.

Net longs in gold futures fell at both COMEX and SHFE, and option traders remained bearish. North American and European gold ETFs still recorded inflows, which the report reads as continued strategic allocation.

The report expects gold to face softer US investor demand and says this could pressure gold lower until an attractive floor is reached. The upcoming Gold Market Commentary on Wed 4 Nov will focus on that floor.

Technical view: gold is testing key support at US$3,858/oz, the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement of the 2015-2026 rise. It is also near a typical downside extreme of 10% below its 200-day average. The bias is to look for a floor on a closing basis. A sustained close below US$3,858/oz would suggest the trend stays lower.

Further support levels are US$3,820/oz, then the 50% retracement of the 2022/2026 rise at US$3,605/oz, with key support at US$3,500/oz. Resistance is US$4,083/oz, and a more secure low needs a move above the 55-day average at US$4,275/oz. The report says positioning has not yet seen a 'positioning washout'.

Tuesday's US midterm elections are in focus. A split Congress is widely expected and could weigh on US equities per a Bloomberg survey, on concerns about tighter AI regulation and gridlock. For gold the impact is mixed: volatility may lift safe-haven demand, while rates and liquidity-driven selling may weigh. Fiscal gridlock could keep term premia elevated, a near-term headwind for gold but supportive of its longer-term case.

The report says strong consensus hiring in October payrolls (Fri) should firm the case for another Fed hike next month, and notes recent Fed comments favour a more gradual pace of tightening. It also says Bloomberg projects a softer payrolls print, so these two statements in the report conflict.

10-year US real yields rejected resistance at 2.92%/3.00%, broke the 55-day average and formed a small top. The report expects the immediate trend in yields to stay lower, with support at 2.47%, then 2.32/2.30% and the 200-day average at 2.20%. Resistance is 2.68% and 2.825%.

The Nasdaq 100 has entered correction territory, 10% down from its peak, as a classic stock/bond correlation returns. Key supports are the 200-day average at 27927, the 38.2% retracement at 28107 and the July low at 27176. A close below 27176 would mark a price top and point to 26182 next.

The Bloomberg DXY remains capped at resistance of 1229/1231, with the 200-week average at 1233. Support is 1218, then the 55-day average at 1209. A sustained hold above 1233 would complete a large base and the report suspects it would be a major headwind for gold.

Macro backdrop for the week: the Fed, ECB and BoJ held rates, Q3 US and Euro-area GDP beat expectations, US PCE inflation stayed elevated with energy up 21% y/y, and China's Fifth Plenum ended with no new stimulus.
earnings_insights: S&P 500 Q3 reporting, already printed: of the 301 companies that have reported, revenue is up 13.64% y/y and EPS up 29.37% y/y. 61% beat revenue estimates and 82% beat earnings expectations. The report does not state whether EPS is adjusted or reported.

Price pressures are persistent and broad-based across goods, with energy up 21% y/y.
Core inflation remains well above target, which supports the hawkish repricing of the Fed path.
Beat expectations and rose from 84.2 in September.
Beat expectations. Spain grew 0.6% and Germany 0.2%, Italy was stable and France contracted 0.1%.
Rates were left unchanged, with the refinancing rate at 2.65%.
Held unchanged, with the BoJ signaling further rate hikes.
Eased from 2.7% in September, with electricity and gas subsidies helping contain prices.
Up from 4.2% in August, taking growth for the first nine months of 2026 to 15.5%. Electronics profits rose 103.8% and autos fell 22.8%.
The report expects a 25 bps hike to the highest level since late 2008, driven by inflation from climbing energy costs.

crypto_views: Bitcoin closed the week at 76,782, down 5.59% w/w and 12.40% y-t-d per the performance table, against a YTD high of 97,922 and low of 58,055.
risk_factors: Leveraged and liquidity-driven selling could push gold lower until an attractive floor is reached.
A sustained close below US$3,858/oz would suggest the immediate downtrend persists, with support next at US$3,820/oz.
A sustained hold above 1233 in the Bloomberg DXY would be a major headwind for gold.
A broader risk-off tone, with the Nasdaq 100 in correction, a close below its July low of 27176 would signal a wider downturn.
Midterm outcome risks: split Congress, tighter AI regulation, gridlock, and elevated term premia.
A further hawkish Fed repricing after strong October payrolls.
Elevated energy costs feeding inflation in the US and Euro area.

tension_points.bull_case: Strategic allocation to gold ETFs continued, with North American and European funds recording inflows. Stickier ETF holders are more positive, and midterm volatility could lift safe-haven demand. Fiscal gridlock could strengthen gold's longer-term case.
tension_points.bear_case: A hawkish repricing of the Fed path drove liquidity-driven selling by leveraged investors, COMEX and SHFE net longs fell, option traders stayed bearish, and the report says no positioning washout has occurred yet. Softer US investor demand could pressure gold lower until a floor is reached.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained close below US$3,858/oz would suggest the immediate trend is likely to remain lower, with support next at US$3,820/oz.

tension_points.bull_case: The Bloomberg DXY remains capped at resistance of 1229/1231 and could stay inside its sideways range if it falls below 1218.
tension_points.bear_case: A sustained hold above 1233 would mark completion of a large base and a change of trend higher for the dollar, which the report suspects would be a major headwind for gold.
